summary: Configured legacy-compatible filesystem snapshots for /srv/data, demonstrated exact rollback after modification, and verified persistence through a node reboot. CentOS 5.11 and kernel 2.6.18-398.el5 were retained.
actions_performed: Installed /usr/local/sbin/data-snapshot using the existing rsync utility.
Stored snapshots under /srv/snapshots/data with SHA-256 manifests.
Overwrote one file, deleted another, changed permissions, and added an unwanted file.
Restored the earlier snapshot and confirmed content and metadata matched exactly.
Restarted node1 once and verified its changed boot identity, SSH recovery, snapshot inventory, and restored data.

evidence.summary: Shows CentOS 5.11, kernel 2.6.18-398.el5, ext3 storage, available rsync, and the unchanged release/kernel after rollback.
Shows the snapshot utility, protected snapshot directories, and initial application data.
Shows snapshot inventory, SHA-256 hashes, ownership, permissions, sizes, and an empty live-versus-snapshot delta.
Proves deliberate divergence, followed by restoration of original files, hashes, permissions, contents, deletion of the extra file, and an empty metadata-aware rsync delta.
Captures the healthy baseline boot ID and data, reboot acknowledgement, changed boot ID, and post-restart SSH, snapshot, data, OS, kernel, and filesystem recovery.
